Made more progress on this project https://github.com/edub0/rcp_esp32_ble_racechrono. It connects the ASL X2 board to the wireless network in the car, converts the Porsche telemetry into canbus and sends it over BLE. I did some load testing, it can do about 500/s BLE notifications, but I think the limitation is actually Racechrono.

I started to explore packing tirex data into BLE frames. Basically I take incoming tirex canbus signals, strip out the temperatures and pack a single canbus payload with 8 zones for one tire. This lets me push tirex over Bluetooth at 16Hz with 4 corners, configured for 8 zones (64 notifications/sec). I could go faster but for now I am leaving Bluetooth bandwidth for the Porsche telemetry.

Extended CAN ID: sensor base + 0x20

 byte       0       1       2       3       4       5       6       7
        +-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
 data   | zone1 | zone2 | zone3 | zone4 | zone5 | zone6 | zone7 | zone8 |
        +-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
 units                   unsigned whole degrees C
 formula        bitsToUintLE(raw, byte_offset * 8, 8)

I started packing other Porsche data as well, for example wheel speeds and tire pressures arrive grouped in a single payload, so packing them doesn't introduce any delay and preserves my BLE bandwidth.
